newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Analyst comment on DSM 96 profit estimate.
newsitem.headline: Analyst comment on DSM 96 profit estimate.

text.p: Chemicals group DSM said on Tuesday it saw full-year 1996 net profit from ordinary operations of at least 700 million guilders.
The preliminary profit figure was well below analysts' consensus of 750.9 million guilders.
Robert Jan Stassen, chemicals analyst at Bangert Pontier -

"The figure as such is slightly disappointing. I had a forecast of 787 million guilders for the year as I had anticipated feedstock costs would weigh less heavily then they have now. DSM raised (selling) prices in September, but it was not possible to raise them again in the fourth quarter..."

"Meanwhile feedstock prices (for oil-based bulk) chemicals, particularly naphtha (the main raw material for plastics), have continued to rise. It depends how much DSM has bought at spot prices and how much on contract...it would seem they have bought relatively more on the short term markets."
Stassen said he maintained a 'Hold' recommendation on DSM, saying it was becoming a more stable company as it moved more downstream into fine chemicals and more tailor-made customer products.
Peter Beijers, analyst at Kempen & Co:

"My initial response is that the figure is rather disappointing -- although not entirely unexpected. The earlier figures from Shell Oil indicated players were having some trouble passing on increases in feedstock prices."

"The trend in itself is not unexpected, but the extent of its impact is." Beijers, who rates the stock a market performer, had been forecasting 1996 earnings of around 750 million guilders, in line with the general consensus.
"It is obviously below expectations...product prices didn't develop as favourably as the company expected, particularly in November and December."

"But the situation has changed substantially...with product prices on the rise in January and February. Economic developments in general are somewhat better this year, giving DSM more basis to increase its selling prices."
"We remain positive on the company and see...profits on the increase again in future. We think 1997 will be a good year for DSM." -- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000, Fax +31 20 504 5040
